. mass intentions: dunboyne. saturday 7pm margaret & john maguire | deceased members of the skelton family | jim & mary lineen & jean lyons. sunday 9am aileen ryan | andrew wall. 11.30am kathleen & bernard higgins. monday 9 am tuesday 9 am wednesday 9am paddy scully | novena mass to end abortion and protect the life of the unborn. thursday 9am gertrude boylan. friday 9am saturday 10 am tommy smith. 7pm sean nealon. sunday 9 am 11.30am the hobbs family | henry & eileen king & deceased family members | martin kirwan | rita & sean reid. intentions: kilbride. saturday 6pm sunday 10 am saturday 6pm paddy clarke. sunday 10 am gerry quinn. paul fitzpatrick, blanchardstown and formerly dunboyne | nicholas kelly, woodview heights | michelle mitchell, whitelands. fr willie doyle tribunal - father doyle was an irish jesuit priest who served as a british army chaplain in world war one and gave his life ministering to soldiers at the battle of passchendaele in 1917. since then, his cult has been strong and bishop tom opened the diocesan tribunal for the cause of his canonisation in 2022 with the approval of the holy see. the investigation has progressed well; the historical commission, the theological investigation and the tribunal itself have now almost concluded. accordingly, the public concluding session of the tribunal will occur after the celebration of vespers in the cathedral of christ the king in mullingar on sunday, october 18" 2026 at 4.00pm. this is the first diocesan tribunal to conclude in ireland for over forty years. after that ceremony, the documentation will be transmitted to the dicastery for the causes of saints in rome. interest in the concluding ceremony is strong and as well as british and irish army representatives, people have informed this office that they will be travelling from the united kingdom and the united states also. all are welcome to attend the celebration of vespers in the cathedral on sunday, october 18" at 4.00pm. the working document for the irish national synodal assembly, taking place in gormanston, co meath, on 17 october, brings together the fruits of five years of prayer, listening and discernment and will guide delegates as they consider and vote on suggested actions to be presented to the bishops of ireland. while the assembly marks an important moment in the journey, the synodal pathway is now moving towards a new phase of implementation. everyone is invited to read, pray with, and reflect on the working document and the question: “what does god want from the church in ireland at this time?” please pray for all those taking part in the assembly and for the guidance of the holy spirit, and scan the qr code to access the working document and find out more, and see
